ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all founding shareholders, directors, UBOs and the prospective master franchisee against (i) the Swiss SECO embargo and sanctions lists, (ii) the consolidated United Nations Security Council sanctions lists, (iii) the EU consolidated financial sanctions list as voluntarily aligned by Switzerland, (iv) the US OFAC SDN list, and (v) the PEP identification standards under AMLA Arts. 3–5 and FINMA Circular 2020/1. Positive PEP or sanctions hits require enhanced due diligence, senior-management approval and, where reportable, an immediate suspicious transaction report to the Swiss Money Laundering Reporting Office (MROS) under AMLA Art. 9.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix – Central Business Name Index (www.zefix.ch), operated by the Federal Commercial Register Office within the Federal Office of Justice, in conjunction with the competent Cantonal Commercial Register Office of the registered-seat canton (e.g., the Commercial Register of the Canton of Zug).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Pursuant to Art. 950 CO, the corporate name must be truthful, distinctive and non-misleading, and must be written in Latin script; Chinese characters are not admissible in the Swiss Commercial Register. The Chinese brand '麻辣烫' must therefore be transliterated and romanized (e.g., 'MALATANG' or 'MA LA TANG') in the articles of association and the register. The full corporate name may be formed in German, French or Italian and must conclude with the legal-form indicator 'Aktiengesellschaft' or 'AG' (or 'Société anonyme'/'SA' where the French form is used).
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Any canton or municipality place name (e.g., 'Zug', 'Zürich', 'Genève') without prior written consent of the relevant authority
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Swiss law does not provide a formal forward name-reservation procedure; the 30-day window reflects the customary validity of the Cantonal Commercial Register's preliminary availability confirmation pending formal filing. Within 30 days of receipt of a rejection decision, the applicant must file a written administrative appeal with the Cantonal Supervisory Authority for Commercial Registers of the seat canton. Further appeals may be lodged successively with the Federal Commercial Register Office at the Federal Office of Justice, the Swiss Federal Administrative Court, and ultimately the Swiss Federal Supreme Court, in accordance with the Federal Act on Administrative Procedure (SR 172.010) and the Commercial Register Ordinance (SR 221.411).

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual or mail-forwarding-only office is impermissible as the registered seat of a commercial fast-casual master-license AG. The registered office must be a genuine physical Swiss address consistent with the company's actual purpose under Art. 611 CO and the Swiss administrative-seat doctrine. A licensed professional domiciliation address may serve only as a supplementary service and mailing address and cannot replace the required physical substance; commercial-register and cantonal tax authorities may otherwise refuse registration or initiate withdrawal or dissolution measures.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 35% probability of an unannounced registered-office and substance verification by the Cantonal Commercial Register supervisory authority or cantonal tax administration within the first 24 months of operation; approximately 55% probability of a physical, unannounced food-safety and hygiene inspection of the licensed Malatang outlet by the Cantonal Food Control Authority under the Swiss Foodstuffs Act (SR 817.0).

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Articles 620–646 and 660 of the Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, CO); Articles 626 ff. CO on incorporation formalities; Article 632 CO on paid-up capital; Articles 178–179 CO on notarial authentication; Articles 936 ff. CO and the Commercial Register Ordinance (HRegV) on registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) at the company's registered seat, functionally supervised by the Federal Commercial Register Office (FEDRO) in Bern.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarially certified Deed of Incorporation and Articles of Association, filed through the commercial register application (Anmeldung zur Eintragung).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The Aktiengesellschaft requires minimum share capital of CHF 100,000. At least 20% of the nominal value of each share, but not less than CHF 50,000 in total, must be paid up in cash before registration, deposited with a Swiss bank in a blocked escrow account. Non-cash contributions must be covered by an audit report as required by Articles 632 and 634 CO.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: At the first meeting of the board of directors of [Company] Aktiengesellschaft, convened at the proposed registered seat, the board unanimously resolved: (1) The deed of incorporation and Articles of Association are approved; (2) The subscription of 1,000 registered shares, each of nominal value CHF 100, is confirmed, and the paid-up capital of CHF 100,000 has been paid in cash and deposited in a Swiss bank escrow account as required by Articles 632 and 634 of the Swiss Code of Obligations; (3) The registered seat is set at [address], Switzerland; (4) [Name] and [Name] are elected directors; [Name] is appointed delegate and authorized to sign singly; (5) The delegate is authorized to procure notarial authentication, commercial register filing, and all ancillary registrations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial Authentication of the Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Notarial Office (Notariat) at the company's registered seat
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the final draft Articles of Association and the list of subscribing shareholders to the notary. The notary verifies the legal identity, capacity, and signatory authority of each shareholder, authenticates the deed in the official cantonal language or English with certified translation, and retains the original for certification transmission.
required_dossiers: Government-issued passports or identity cards of founding shareholders
Name reservation confirmation from the Commercial Register Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary queries the deed, cure by correcting the Articles, obtaining a certified translation, or filing a revised name reservation without additional charge.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit and Verification of Paid-up Capital in Escrow
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss bank authorized by FINMA, supported by the notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked share capital account (Sperrkonto) in the name of the company being formed and transfer at least CHF 50,000 from the aggregate share subscription. The bank issues a written confirmation of payment and blocking to the notary. The notary verifies the amount against the share register before drafting the notarial closing statement.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the capital verification certificate is rejected, instruct the bank to correct the escrow form, deposit any shortfall, or obtain a new blocked account certificate and re-file with the notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing with the Cantonal Commercial Register Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarially certified application for entry, including the authenticated deed, proof of capital, list of directors with specimen signatures and powers of attorney. Pay the registration fee and await entry in the cantonal register. The registration is transmitted electronically to the Federal Commercial Register Office.
required_dossiers: List of directors and authorized signatories
Notice to the tax authority if a real estate seat is registered
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, cure the defect by filing a supplementary submission with the Commercial Register within the statutory deadline, resubmit corrected specimen signatures, or apply for a formal amendment of the registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, the Commercial Register Office transmits the entry to the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce. The company verifies the published capital, legal form, registered office, and authorized signatories. Any shareholder liability or disclosure requirement becomes effective as of publication.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication contains an error, file a correction request with the Commercial Register Office, which will issue a corrective publication at no additional official fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with Tax and Social Security Authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration; Federal Tax Administration (ESTV); Compensation Office (Ausgleichskasse)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the official commercial register extract and incorporation deed to the cantonal tax administration for corporate income tax and VAT purposes; register with the federal VAT authorities if taxable revenue is expected; register as an employer with the cantonal OASI compensation office. Ensure corporate tax pre-payments are scheduled.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any authority requires supplementary data, provide the missing declarations through the single electronic portal or apply for a statutory extension before penalty accrual.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Cantonal Department of Economic Affairs and Labour (Amt für Wirtschaft und Arbeit / Service de l'économie et du travail) and Municipal Trade Office (Gewerbeamt).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Restaurant and take-away operating permit (Betriebsbewilligung für Gastgewerbe) issued by the Canton, together with the food business operator approval under the cantonal food control ordinance.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN/BAFU) and competent cantonal environmental agency
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category: Exempt from a full EIA for a fast-casual food service outlet under the Swiss Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (UVPV) Annex; a simple environmental registration with the cantonal agency is required before operation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater must be pre-treated with grease separators and oil traps in accordance with the Waters Protection Ordinance (GSchV); cooking emissions must be filtered so that oily aerosols and volatile organic compounds meet the Clean Air Ordinance (LRV) thresholds; food waste and hazardous kitchen waste must be handled and disposed of under the Waste Ordinance (VVEA).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Fire Police or Cantonal Fire Insurance Authority; structural load inspection certification for the listed premises; workplace safety clearance from Suva for commercial kitchen equipment; occupational health and hygiene clearance for food-contact surfaces and ventilation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (FTA / Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions AFC), Eigerstrasse 65, 3003 Bern; official portal: www.estv.admin.ch; e-Service VAT portal: www.estv.admin.ch/e-services (VAT registration, returns, payments and correspondence).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Incorporate the AG by notarial deed, pay in at least CHF 50,000 of the CHF 100,000 minimum share capital, and register in the Cantonal Commercial Register of the registered office canton. 2. The UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer / IDE / IDI, format CHE-###.###.###) is automatically issued by the Federal Statistical Office upon commercial register publication; no separate UID application is required for a Swiss-resident AG. 3. For a non-established foreign entity, a Swiss fiscal representative must be appointed and an UID obtained via the FTA in the course of VAT registration. 4. Submit the VAT registration application (Formular Aufnahme der Steuerpflicht) through the FTA e-Service portal, attaching the commercial register extract, articles of association and, for the franchise master licence business, the master franchise and licence agreements evidencing the Swiss supply chain. 5. The FTA assigns the VAT number (MWST-Nr / N° TVA / No. IVA), typically identical to the UID with the suffix MWST/TVA/IVA; the same UID constitutes the corporate TIN for direct federal and cantonal tax purposes, and the AG must thereafter file annual Swiss VAT returns, submit statutory financial statements, and comply with cantonal tax return requirements for federal, cantonal and communal income/capital tax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; Swiss AG is a resident corporation subject to unlimited tax liability at federal, cantonal and communal levels. Federal corporate income tax applies at a flat rate of 8.5% (computed on profit after tax) plus cantonal/communal income and capital taxes (combined effective rate approx. 11-22% depending on canton); foreign permanent establishments and foreign real estate are exempt with progression; no passthrough election exists for an AG.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Swiss law does not recognise a US-style check-the-box or transparent entity election; entity-level taxation is mandatory. Available elections under Swiss law: (1) VAT group taxation election (Art. 21 MWSTG) for financially, economically and organisationally integrated entities to be treated as a single VAT taxpayer; (2) flat-rate 'saldo' VAT method election (Art. 37 MWSTG) permitting simplified input VAT deduction by sector-specific rates; (3) voluntary VAT registration below the CHF 100,000 turnover threshold (Art. 11 MWSTG); (4) option to tax an otherwise exempt real-estate supply (Art. 22 MWSTG); (5) hybrid mismatch rules (Art. 61a/62a DBG) are mandatory and cannot be neutralised by election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Swiss Value Added Tax (VAT / Mehrwertsteuer / TVA / IVA) under the Federal Act on Value Added Tax of 12 June 2009 (SR 641.20). Standard rate 8.1%, reduced rate 2.6% (food and non-alcoholic beverages for home consumption, including take-away food), special accommodation rate 3.8%.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 of annual worldwide turnover from taxable supplies (excluding exempt supplies and certain real-estate proceeds) for businesses established in Switzerland; non-established foreign suppliers register at CHF 100,000 of annual turnover from taxable supplies with a Swiss nexus (Art. 10 MWSTG). Licence and royalty turnover from the Malatang self-serve franchise master licensing counts as taxable turnover for threshold purposes.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, state API or digital stamping regime applies in Switzerland. VAT invoices must contain the mandatory particulars of Art. 26 MWSTG (supplier identity and UID/VAT number, recipient, date, goods/services, consideration, VAT rate and tax amount). Electronic invoicing is lawful; the Swiss QR-bill (QR-Rechnung) and Peppol BIS 3.0 are the adopted standards. From 2026, suppliers to Swiss federal authorities must issue and receive structured e-invoices under the Federal E-Invoicing Ordinance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: 0% VAT with full input VAT deduction applies where goods are dispatched or transported by the supplier or a third party to a foreign destination (Art. 23 para. 1 no. 1 MWSTG). Services and intangibles: zero rating applies to B2B supplies to entrepreneurial recipients with seat or place of business abroad, services relating to foreign real estate, and transfers of licences, brand rights, know-how and intellectual property used exclusively abroad (Art. 23 para. 2 MWSTG). For the Chinese Malatang self-serve master franchise licence, offshore royalty and franchise fee income is zero rated where the foreign franchisee is an entrepreneur and the licensed exploitation rights are located and used outside Switzerland; domestic on-premise restaurant turnover of the Swiss AG is taxable at 8.1% and take-away food at 2.6%, with no zero rating applicable to domestic food service. Switzerland imposes no statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (e-dec Ausfuhrzollanmeldung) validated by the Swiss Federal Customs Administration, including the export summary document for the exporting AG
Transport document evidencing physical export: Bill of Lading (sea), CMR waybill (road) or Air Waybill (air) naming the Swiss exporter as shipper and a foreign destination
Commercial invoice stating 'Export / Zero Rated VAT Art. 23 MWSTG' and bearing the Swiss UID/VAT number
Inward remittance certificate or banking records evidencing receipt of export proceeds in foreign currency

For franchise/licence exports: written master franchise contract, royalty schedule, foreign franchisee VAT-registration or tax-residence proof, and a signed declaration that the licensed intellectual property is exploited outside Switzerland
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The FTA's export-control and VAT audit sections cross-check customs export declarations, transport documents, invoice flows and bank receipts. Where zero rating is not substantiated, the FTA retroactively reassesses VAT at the standard or reduced rate (8.1%/2.6%, or 3.8% for accommodation-related supplies), adds default interest of 4.5-5% per annum, and applies a 10-year reassessment limitation period. Penalties under Arts. 101-103 MWSTG: wilful and deceitful tax fraud carries a fine of up to CHF 250,000 and/or imprisonment; less serious wilful infringements carry a fine of up to CHF 35,000; negligent violations carry a fine of up to CHF 5,000; the evaded tax and interest are collected in addition, and administrative publication or forfeiture of the tax advantage may be ordered in serious cases.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB) in conjunction with the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA) for regulatory oversight and the Federal Department of Finance (FDF) for trade reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Swiss franc (CHF) is fully convertible on both current and capital account. Switzerland maintains no exchange controls or restrictions on payments, transfers, or profit remittances, subject to general anti-money laundering (AML) and sanctions compliance. Profit repatriation to foreign shareholders is unrestricted; dividends, royalties, and interest may be remitted via any licensed bank without prior SNB approval, though companies must comply with Swiss withholding tax procedures (e.g., 35% withholding tax on dividends, reduced under applicable treaty). No quantitative limits exist on cross-border fund flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory requirement exists to surrender export proceeds or convert foreign currency receipts into CHF. Exporters may retain funds in any freely convertible currency. SNB does not mandate conversion ratios or timelines. All proceeds are subject to standard banking transaction reporting for statistics and AML purposes, but there is no mandatory conversion deadline.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Credit Suisse (now part of UBS Switzerland AG under integration)
Julius Bär (private banking focus, selective for corporate franchise entities)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (for higher-net intra-group liquidity)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-Low for foreign offshore digital EMI-only structures (e.g., UK/EU EMIs) due to FINMA licensing requirements for deposit-taking and payment services. FINMA awards a 'Fintech License' (banking license relaxation) for public deposits up to CHF 100m, but pure payment service providers need a 'PI License' under the Financial Institutions Act (FinIA). Offshore EMIs can partner with Swiss correspondent banks, however, Swiss licensed banks often reject EMIs without a local physical presence. Recommended route: incorporate a Swiss finance subsidiary or obtain FinIA license for higher compliance viability.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Swiss banks generally require face-to-face identification of the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO), directors, and signatories during the onboarding interview. Remote video identification is accepted only where the bank has an approved digital onboarding process (FINMA-compliant) and the client jurisdiction is low-risk, but in practice the majority of Tier-1 Swiss banks mandate a physical appearance at a Swiss branch for non-resident companies. Attendance by at least one local resident director (or an authorised local representative with notarised power of attorney) is typically required; full remote opening for an offshore-controlled company is rare and subject to enhanced due diligence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident corporate structure with multiple jurisdictions (e.g., holding company in another country, Swiss AG subsidiary).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide organisational chart with shareholding trail, certified corporate registry extracts (e.g., Swiss Commercial Register and overseas equivalent), letter of explanation for corporate purpose, audited financial statements of the parent, comprehensive source-of-wealth documentation, and references from a recognised bank or law firm.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business model of 'Chinese Malatang Self-Serve' franchise in the fast-casual food sector, perceived as high-volume cash-intensive operations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Present notarised franchise agreements, revenue processing contracts with POS providers, estimated cash-flow forecasts, AML risk assessment of the franchise network, and a detailed liquidity trail showing payment flows via bank transfers and regulated payment gateways rather than cash.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ownership by non-resident beneficial owners resident in or with funds originating from higher-risk jurisdictions (e.g., China).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provision of certified passport copies, proof of residence and tax residence certificates, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation (e.g., sale of property, employment, prior business), and a sworn affidavit confirming beneficial ownership. In addition, obtain a pre-screening opinion from a Swiss independent AML advisor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Signing authority designated to nominees, powers of attorney, or fiduciaries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide notarised power of attorney document, identity of each attorney with UBO disclosure, and a durable written explanation for the fiduciary arrangement. Bank may require a physical meeting with the actual UBO rather than the nominee.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Borrowing or intercompany financing from related parties triggering thin-capitalisation or transfer-pricing scrutiny.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Maintain arm's-length loan agreement with interest rate determination, group transfer-pricing documentation, updated Swiss financial statements, and evidence of compliance with OECD TP guidelines. Provide the bank with a copy of the group structure and loan rationale.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections into the Swiss AG must be routed via SWIFT MT103 (wire transfer) or SEPA (if within EU/EEA and in EUR) using the corporate account IBAN at a licensed Swiss bank. The correct purpose codes must be used to align with Swiss reporting: for equity contributions, use purpose code A10 (equity injection) or B20 (non-export trade; capital under Swiss Payment Statistics). For shareholder loans use C10 (loan repayment/outflow) and C20 (loan disbursement). The bank may require a notarised board resolution authorising the capital injection, proof of funds, and a subscription agreement to evidence compliance with minimum capital requirements (AG minimum CHF 100,000). For foreign direct investment (FDI) from non-EU residents, banking verification includes SNB statistical reporting (R1 form) and the bank will ask for a compliance declaration. Proceeds must be booked in CHF unless otherwise agreed and should be accompanied by a copy of the Commercial Register entry and payment reference to the share capital account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements (e.g., royalty payments, equipment procurement, supplier payments for the franchise operation) should use SWIFT MT103 (single funds transfer) or MT202 (bank-to-bank) for USD/EUR transactions. For trade finance where goods constitute a cross-border transaction, a commercial Letter of Credit (LC) issued by the Swiss bank is acceptable, though standard practice for fast-casual franchise payments will be an LC at sight or deferred payment LC. The beneficiary's correspondent bank and account must be fully verified to avoid sanctions screening delays. Clarification of the payment message must include the Swiss purpose code (e.g., B09 for services, B30 for royalties) and an invoice number. SEPA direct debit is limited to B2B within EEA/EU and is not permitted for Swiss law-governed contracts; use SEPA credit transfer (SCT) or SWIFT. For high-frequency royalty payments, a bank-liaised 'payment gateway' via a licensed Swiss payment provider (e.g., Clearstream, Securites) may be used, but all fees must be documented for transfer-pricing compliance.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Forward contracts (up to 12 months, tenor extension permitted) for hedging CHF/USD or CHF/EUR royalty and invoice flows
FX swaps (swap of principal and interest in two currencies) for managing intercompany liquidity
Short-dated options (calls/puts) on CHF pairs sold over the counter by the Swiss bank, subject to FINMA derivatives regulations
Interest rate swaps (basis risk swaps) where the underlying debt is CHF- or USD-denominated (often paired with an FX swap)

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) are permissible only for exotic currency exposure that lacks a liquid onshore forward market (e.g., CNY), though Swiss banks treat them as OTC derivatives requiring ISDA documentation and daily margin
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) for long-term intercompany lending (e.g., 5-year fixed-to-fixed) to transform a foreign currency loan into CHF, alongside hedge accounting under Swiss GAAP
Executing FX hedges must be done via a licensed bank or broker with FINMA registration; no exchange approval needed for CHF pairs, but transactions exceeding CHF 50m are reported to SNB

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income and Capital Tax Return (Steuererklärung der juristischen Personen)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration (Kantonale Steuerverwaltung) and Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after fiscal year-end; for 31 December year-end generally due 30 September, extendable on application
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest accrues; late-filing penalty up to 30% of assessed tax or CHF 10,000; estimated assessment and forced collection; continued non-compliance may be reported to the commercial register for dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV), VAT Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Quarterly within 60 days after quarter-end; semi-annual or annual return when small-taxpayer procedure applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Arrears interest at 4% p.a.; penalty up to CHF 8,000 per violation; VAT evasion surcharge of up to three times the evaded tax.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM) approval of annual financial statements and board reports
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' meeting; the minutes and accounts are retained at the registered office and submitted to tax administrations only upon request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after fiscal year-end (Art. 699 para 2 OR); for 31 December year-end, by 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Shareholders may compel convening in court; directors face civil liability for losses; persistent failure invalidates corporate organization and can lead to declaratory dissolution under Art. 731b OR.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Share Register and Beneficial Ownership annual verification (Aktienregister)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered office (company's corporate records); no filing to Commercial Register except on share-capital changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuous update upon each transfer; annual internal audit and confirmation at the AGM date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors' personal liability; fines under Swiss Criminal Code for false bookkeeping/forging; suspension of membership rights for shareholders not registered in periodic register.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary audit mandatory if two of three thresholds exceeded for two consecutive years: total assets CHF 20 million, net turnover CHF 40 million, 250 average employees. Otherwise limited audit required unless all shareholders waive and company has no more than 10 employees.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (OR) accounting provisions; Swiss GAAP FER for presentation; IFRS optional for statutory accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No separate public UBO annual return. For bearer shares, the company maintains and updates a register of beneficial owners upon any acquisition or transfer; for registered shares, the Aktienregister contains owner details. The Board confirms the registers' accuracy and completeness at each AGM; changes to registered capital or shareholders of bearer shares trigger a commercial register filing.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Bearer Share Register and Beneficial Owners Register (Inhaberaktienregister) when bearer shares exist
Minute Book of the General Meeting (Protokoll der Generalversammlung)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $1,200–$3,500 for registered office and corporate domicile secretarial service
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $2,500–$6,000 for limited audit; $6,000–$15,000 for ordinary audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% federal standard corporate income tax (tax-on-tax; approximately 9.3% pre-tax equivalent) plus cantonal and communal taxes, producing a combined effective tax rate of approximately 11.9%–21.0% depending on canton and activity; Zug and other holding-friendly cantons commonly yield 14%–16% for licensing/franchise companies.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory cantonal tax holidays for newly established companies in certain cantons (e.g., Neuchâtel, Valais) up to 10 years; federal and cantonal participation relief for qualifying dividend and capital gains income; R&D super-deduction up to 150% in certain cantons for qualifying Swiss R&D costs; patent box or invention deduction granting 10%–90% exemption on IP royalty income depending on canton; holding company privilege for pure holding subsidiaries; no deemed income taxation of unrepatriated foreign profits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Cantonal corporate income tax return for legal entities (Steuererklärung juristische Personen / Déclaration fiscale pour personnes morales), filed electronically through the canton's e-filing portal (e.g., eTax ZG in Zug, ZH eTax in Zurich, VAG in Geneva); federal direct tax assessment is integrated into the same cantonal return. VAT, if applicable, is filed via the Swiss Federal Tax Administration portal SwissComTax.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (taxation by assessment); provisional corporate income tax and social security contributions are payable quarterly; no separate quarterly corporate income tax return is required.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return must be filed by 31 March following the fiscal year-end, unless the cantonal tax authority grants an extension (generally up to 6 months by request); non-resident companies with a permanent establishment must file in the canton where the PE is registered and on the prescribed canton-specific form.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification: legal name, registered seat, UID/CHE number, cantonal tax jurisdiction, and primary ISIC/NACE activity code, including 5610 for fast-casual food operation and master licensing.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For foreign companies, identify the Swiss permanent establishment (address, branch registry number, UID, and tax representative) and do not complete this box with the foreign head-office address.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal form and corporate data: Aktiengesellschaft (AG/SA), share capital (minimum CHF 100,000), date of incorporation, and status of franchise/master-licensing operations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Specify 'foreign corporation acting through Swiss permanent establishment' and attach a copy of the Swiss branch registration and fiscal power of attorney.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: General information: fiscal year-end, accounting currency, VAT status, business restructuring, and list of related parties in the franchise chain.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the PE opening/closing dates and confirm whether the head-office jurisdiction applies a DTA that restricts Swiss taxing rights to PE income under Article 7.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance sheet summary: assets, liabilities, receivables from shareholders, and franchise rights or master licensing intangible assets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter only Swiss PE assets; if capital allocation is not separately booked, provide the arm's length net equity allocation methodology used for the PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue: restaurant sales, self-serve broth bowl sales, franchise royalties, master license fees, sub-licence fees, and incidental income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only Swiss-source PE revenue; if royalty income arises from a Swiss franchisee, determine whether the PE in Switzerland performs the relevant licensing franchise activities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses: cost of raw materials, food ingredients, staff wages, lease, utilities, maintenance, depreciation, and amortization of master license rights.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only expenses economically connected to the Swiss PE and apply an appropriate and documented overhead allocation key; cross-border allocations must be supported by transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Royalty and licensing activity data: amounts received from Chinese or other foreign franchisees for use of the Malatang brand, recipes, know-how, and self-serve system.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the foreign IP holder merely collects royalties without Swiss functions, no Swiss PE should be reported; but if Swiss-based staff conclude contracts, enforce rights, or assume risk, a taxable presence may exist and royalties must be allocated to Switzerland.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustments and non-deductible expenses: add-back of corporate income tax, excessive management fees, royalty payments to low-tax jurisdictions, interest on excessive shareholder debt, and undocumented entertainment expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back interest and royalties paid to foreign head office that are not at arm's length, and ensure no deduction is claimed for Swiss withholding tax that is not economically borne by the PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reliefs and incentives: participation income exemption, R&D super-deduction, patent box deduction, and prior-year loss carryforward utilization.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim participation or IP box relief only if the Swiss PE holds the qualifying rights or shareholdings and performs the relevant management functions; attach the required evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit/loss and assessment basis: final determination of Swiss federal and cantonal taxable profit, including allocation between federal and cantonal tax years.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute Swiss PE taxable profit on an arm's length basis using the authorized OECD approach; apply Swiss loss carryforward not exceeding seven years and attach a detailed PE profit and loss statement.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a procedural fine of approximately CHF 50–CHF 500 per month of delay, plus default interest at annual rates of about 3%–5% on the assessed tax, accruing daily. Persistent failure results in a taxable-assessment-by-estimate, denial of deductions without sufficient proof, and, for intentional evasion, criminal proceedings with fines up to three times the evaded tax and imprisonment up to two years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% statutory Swiss withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) on dividends paid by the Swiss AG to any shareholder, whether resident or non-resident, unless a double tax treaty or Swiss domestic participation privilege reduces the effective burden.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a DTA-reduced dividend rate, the Swiss company must file a relief at source application with the Swiss Federal Tax Administration using Form 858 (KAE-Erklärung) before making the distribution. For treaty refunds, the non-resident beneficial owner must submit the relevant Swiss DTA refund claim form (e.g., Form 823 for US, Form 824 for Germany, Form 824-CH for China) within three years after the dividend payment, together with an annual Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the foreign tax authority, a shareholding certificate, beneficial ownership declaration, and evidence of economic substance sufficient to satisfy the Principal Purpose Test under the MLI.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: Swiss domestic law imposes no withholding tax on royalty payments; treaties generally apply 0%–10% for royalties, with the People's Republic of China–Switzerland DTA providing a 10% rate on copyright/industrial royalties absent a permanent establishment. Interest: Swiss domestic law generally imposes no withholding tax on ordinary commercial debt interest, but a 35% statutory withholding tax applies to interest from Swiss bank deposits, Swiss bond issues, money-market instruments, and similar movable capital in specific cases; DTA rates for bond interest usually range from 0% to 15%, while interest from related-party commercial loans is commonly tax-free at treaty level to a bona fide beneficial owner.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: The Swiss Federal Tax Administration expects contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation, corresponding to a Local File, where annual cross-border related-party transactions involving goods, services, royalties, or financing by the Swiss entity exceed CHF 5 million per year; a Master File is expected when the multinational group has aggregate global turnover exceeding CHF 1 billion. Even below these thresholds, arm's length evidence is required if intercompany transactions exist.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland does not apply Cayman- or Barbados-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR), but economic substance is a foundational condition for Swiss tax residence, treaty relief, and the arm's length principle. A Swiss AG holding or licensing Chinese Malatang brand rights must demonstrate, in Switzerland, real personnel, decision-making, contract negotiation, royalty management, bank accounts, and IP enforcement functions. If substance is lacking, the Swiss tax authority may reattribute royalty income to the offshore parent or treat the Swiss entity as an agent of the foreign principal; the MLI Principal Purpose Test and Swiss GAAR (Art. 21 DBG / General anti-avoidance rule) can deny treaty benefits where the main purpose is obtaining tax relief. For the fast-casual self-serve franchise model, the Swiss master licensor must retain economic substance commensurate with its contractual functions and IP risks.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and False Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating Swiss taxable income in the corporate tax return, disguising profit distributions as loans, recording fictitious franchise costs, inflating head-office service charges, or using hidden bank accounts for royalty fees from Chinese and other franchisees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Art. 175 DBG, a fine may be imposed up to three times the amount of tax evaded but not less than CHF 1,000; default interest of 3.5% per annum on evaded tax; exclusion of deductions; and in severe cases criminal imprisonment up to two years under Art. 176 DBG for attempted qualified tax fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or cause the filing of a false return, or who knowingly conceal income from the franchise/IP model, are personally jointly and severally liable for the underpaid tax and fine if they acted intentionally or negligently; Swiss corporate law (Art. 754 CO) allows creditor and shareholder claims for damages, and tax authorities may seek civil restitution, travel restrictions, and disqualification from board functions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Withhold Swiss Withholding Tax on Dividends
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends, parent-subsidiary payments, or Swiss-source bond interest without deducting the statutory 35% Swiss withholding tax, or failing to obtain a KAE authorization before paying a reduced treaty dividend, including a disguised upstream loan or excessive repayment of capital treated as taxable dividend.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Swiss company is liable for the unwithheld tax amount; a late payment penalty and default interest are assessed; if intentional, criminal tax fraud proceedings can impose fines and imprisonment; the recipient loses treaty relief and may suffer double taxation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for unwithheld tax if they knowingly instructed or failed to ensure the tax deduction under Art. 12 VStG; piercing the veil is permitted when the company is frustrated or knowingly participates; civil restitution claims may cover the full withholding amount and penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Misstatement and Shell Substance Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Pricing Chinese Malatang trademark royalties and self-serve system license fees to the Swiss master franchisor without an established independent pricing model; charging no royalty or an artificially low royalty to related foreign franchisees; using a Swiss-registered dossier without staff, premises, economic activity, or TP records; or allocating IP risk to a tax-haven shell while operations are managed in Switzerland or China.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Swiss tax authorities may make a transfer pricing adjustment under Art. 58 DBG, recharacterizing income and disallowing excess deductions; additional federal and cantonal tax of up to 21% combined effective rate applies, plus annual default interest of 3.5%; failure to provide the required TP documentation can trigger administrative fines up to CHF 10,000 and the application of penalties for intentional evasion; DTA relief may be denied under the Principal Purpose Test.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who adopted or approved non-arm's length intercompany royalty rates, failed to maintain contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation, or engaged in a sham structure can be personally liable for resulting tax adjustments and penalties; civil liability includes reimbursement of the company's tax cost and loss to minority shareholders; an administrative investigation may lead to an international travel ban and criminal prosecution for aiding tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company Formation and Economic Substance Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Swiss AG and the Chinese Malatang master-license sub-holding structure as a pure letterbox with no physical office, no local employees, no board meetings in Switzerland, no independent risk management, no real operating bank account, and all key decisions being made in China or another foreign jurisdiction solely to access the Swiss-China DTA and Swiss withholding tax relief.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Swiss GAAR may deem the shell entity not to be the beneficial owner of the royalty and dividend streams, causing the reattribution of income to the foreign principal, denial of DTA benefits, full Swiss-based taxation of the deemed Swiss PE, and fines for violation of correct bookkeeping; the commercial registrar may strike the entity from the register if it is found to have no statutory seat or administrative activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the shell are exposed to personal liability for DTA relief fraud; civil restitution to the tax authorities for unpaid Swiss tax and interest; criminal sanctions for facilitating tax evasion and money laundering; travel bans, asset freezes, and prohibition from managing legal entities in Switzerland; veil piercing is consented where the company is a mere façade.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering and AML Beneficial Ownership Non-Disclosure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting Swiss or international franchise investments in cash or through unqualified intermediaries without compliance with the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act (AMLA), failing to identify the ultimate beneficial owner of the AG and the Chinese parent, or routing periodic royalty/franchise payments through opaque foreign trusts or nominee accounts to conceal the ownership of the business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Breach of AML obligations can result in a fine of up to CHF 500,000 for serious cases, confiscation of the illicitly gained assets, and imprisonment up to three years under Swiss Criminal Code Art. 305bis; the company may be denied DTA refunds and face enhanced tax audit scrutiny; the regulator can close the Swiss unit for continued non-compliance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and AML compliance officers face personal criminal liability if they knowingly accept or process funds of criminal origin; civil liability under AMLA and the Swiss Code of Obligations includes restitution of the assets plus interest; travel bans, extradition, and reputational debarment are common; all directors who fail to report suspicious franchise payment flows may be held jointly liable for consequent tax and criminal sanctions.
